explanation: Strips cut from the papyrus stem were laid in two crossing layers, then pressed and dried into sheets. The word paper comes from papyrus, through Greek and Latin.

claims.text: Ancient Egyptians made their main writing material from the papyrus plant.
Bamboo, flax and lotus were not the source of ancient Egypt's main writing material.
Papyrus sheets were made from strips of the plant's stem laid in two crossing layers, pressed and dried.
The English word paper comes from papyrus, through Greek and Latin.

evidence.restatement: Egypt's chief writing material, papyrus, was made from the papyrus sedge, Cyperus papyrus.
Bamboo slips were a Chinese writing material, flax was spun into linen and the lotus was never a writing material, so none of them was ancient Egypt's main one.
Thin strips of papyrus pith were laid side by side, a second layer was laid across them at right angles, and the sheet was pressed and dried.
